BiblicalUsage: The word means to wrap up, and it is used for a prophet hiding his face, a sword kept in cloth, and a covering over the nations. Elijah wrapped his face in his mantle when he heard the still small voice at Horeb, and David took Goliath's sword, wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod, when he fled from Saul. Isaiah says God will destroy the covering cast over all people.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe wrapping marks both reverence and hiding: Elijah covered his face before a holy God, and men wrap what they fear to show. I hold that God Himself will unwrap the covering over the nations, so what was hidden will be seen plainly at last.
